results.reason: Item 1 explains that §9.4(c) removes the cap and basket for all §9.2(a) rep claims. It says every rep breach is therefore uncapped, beyond the $1.84M escrow, and redrafts the carve-out to cover only Fundamental Representations and Fraud.

Item 4 identifies the Delaware law and forum conflict, notes the split-forum risk, and recommends conforming the TSA to New York. It never explains that APA §10.12 lets the TSA control as to its own subject matter, so the conflict is not cured. The §10.12 analysis appears only for the Bill of Sale.

Item 2 shows the BoS definition has no Excluded Asset carve-out and would convey cash, Albany and HOLLIS. It explains §10.12's specific-subject-matter exception and recommends adopting the APA definition with express exclusions.
The memo states the 10% cap ($1,840,000) and ties it to the escrow.
The memo identifies cash, the Albany manufacturing facility and the HOLLIS trademark as Excluded Assets under §2.2.
Each item gives a 'Where' with sections, explains the issue and its significance to the Seller, and gives a 'Fix'.
Issues are ordered 'Most Significant First' with severity labels, and Section 4 lists items requiring business decisions.
The memo argues §10.12 lets the BoS control and proposes narrowing it. It never claims §10.12 cures either conflict.
The memo concludes that rep-breach exposure is uncapped, not limited to the cap or escrow.
